4. It appears from the impugned order that the petitioner produced copy of the judgment dated 11-4-1960 passed in Title Suit No. 180 of 1958 and judgment dated 31-5-1961 passed in Title Appeal No.306 of 1960 before the respondent No. 2 who on consideration of the CS Map and ROR Khatian found that disputed Jalmahal was recorded in the name of the Government in khatian No. 1 and Plot No.1448 and by mistake area was recorded as .38 acres though actually area was 65.38 acres. Respondent No. 2 further found that the fishery in question was not excavated by the petitioner but it is a natural fishery. So he held that the petitioner has no right to hold the said fishery under the provisions of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He further found that Ordinance No. XII of 1960 came into operation on 17-6-1960. Sub-section 2(a) was added in section 20 of the said Act by the said Ordinance and under the said provisions decree obtained by the petitioner in respect of the disputed fishery has become infructuous. He further found that compensation assessment roll in respect of Akhakhora Mouja in which the fishery in question is situated was finally published on 3-3-1962 and, as such, the said fishery vested in the Government in spite of the aforesaid judgment and decree in favour of the petitioner. 

 6. Sub-section (1) of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides that On the acquisition of interest of rent receivers in ant area under Chapter V, no rent receiver, cultivating raiyat, cultivating under raiyat or non-agricultural tenant shall be entitled to retain possession of any of his khas lands in such area except as provided in sub-section (2) 

 8. Petitioner has produced before us an information slip supplied by the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Habigonj on 3-1-1990 (Annexure-H). It appears from the said information slip that no compensation was assessed in respect of the disputed plot No. 1448 in part 'Kha' of the compensation assessment roll. It appears from Form X of the State Acquisition Rules 1951 that compensation assessment roll is prepared in 2 parts-part-A and Part-B. Part A relates to compensation for the rent receiving interests and part B relates to Khas lands, Rule 54 of the said rules provides for preparation of compensation assessment roll in respect of khas land of Clauses (b)(d) and (d-I) mentioned in section 39 (1) of the said Act. Clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 39 of the Act provides for payment of compensation for acquisition of land consisting of fishery or forest or land used for a ferry at the rate of five times the net annual profit from such land. From the above information slip and above provisions it appears that compensation assessment roll for the rayoti interest of petitioner in the disputed fishery has not yet been prepared. 

 9. In the case of Shah Md. Elias vs. Province of East Pakistan reported in 17 DLR 277 it has been held: "A close reading of the above provisions point to inevitable conclusions, firstly, that every interest which is liable to be acquired under the Act has to be paid for and, secondly that except in the cases of acquisition under Chapter II of the Act the interests which are acquirable vest in the Provincial Government only if assessment of compensation in regard to the same has been made and published as provided in the Act. It was further held: "In that view of the matter it cannot be contended that the said lands have vested in the Government as they are acquirable and that there has been a notification in respect of that area under section 43(2) of the Act. The aforesaid judgment was delivered by a Division Bench of the then Dhaka High Court on 10-8-1964 over-looking the decision of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of Province of East Pakistan vs. Muktagacha Abbasia Senior Madrasha reported in 16 DLR (SC) 281; In that case it has been held: 

 "Sub-section (1) of section 20 clearly affects the rights of also a raiyat, a cultivating under raiyat and even a non-agricultural tenant and seems to indicate that as a consequence of the acquisition of the rent receiving interest even khas lands can not be retained except as provided in sub-section (2) of section 20, no matter by whom they are held." 

 "So far as rent receivers are concerned their interest, are to vest either from the date of notification of acquisition or from the date mentioned in such a notification. But so far as tenants were concerned, their interests are to stand acquired and vested in the Government on the notification of the final publication of the compensation assessment roll." 

 10. We have already notice that sub-section, (1) of section 20 provides that no raiyat shall be entitled to retain possession of any khas land on the acquisition of interest of rent receivers in any area under Chapter V. Chapter V provided for preparation of compensation assessment roll. Section 32 to section 46 are included in Chapter V Section 42 of the Act provides for final publication of the compensation assessment roll. Section 43 of the Act provides for publishing a notification declaring that compensation assessment roll in respect of any village or group of villages or local area has been finally published. Sub-section (3) of section 44 of the Act provides that all interests of rayats etc. in non-retainable khas land other than the interest which has already been acquired under any other provision of the Act i.e. section 3 under Chapter II or sub-section (3) of section 46 E shall be deemed to have been acquired by the Government and vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication in the official Gazette. On the other hand, sub-section (1) of the said section 44 provides that all interest of rent receivers in the estates, tenures and all other rent receiving interests in any holding or tenancy or in the non-retainable khas land other than the interest already acquired under Chapter II or sub-section (3) of section 46E shall be deemed to have been acquired by the Government and vest absolutely in the Government from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification in the official Gazette. Thus reading sections 20, 43 and 44 of the Act together we have no option but to hold that non-retainable khas land belonging either to the rent receiver or to the tenant shall be deemed to have been acquired by the Government and vested in the Government with the publication of a notification about final publication of the compensation assessment roll in the official Gazette from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification. Though section 39 of the Act provides for payment of compensation to the tenants also, non-preparation and non-publication of the compensation assessment roll in respect of tenant's interest in such land can not detain the Government from taking over possession of the non-retainable khas lands of the tenants after final publication of compensation assessment roll in respect of the landlord's interest of such tenanted land.
